skills.description: Harness engineering is the discipline of building the systems around AI agents — tools, memory, context windows, permissions, verification steps, recovery paths, and feedback loops — that make agents reliable in production. It represents the shift from prompt engineering (changing inputs) to engineering the entire operational environment.
skills.use_case: Building production-grade AI agents that reliably handle complex, long-running tasks without silent failures or runaway costs
skills.output: Reliable AI agent systems that self-correct, recover from errors, and operate within defined constraints
tips: Focus on tools, memory, permissions, verification, and recovery paths — not just prompts
Microsoft's Retrospective Harness Optimization paper (arxiv 2606.05922) formalizes this approach
Microsoft Work IQ APIs provide a new context layer for AI agents working on business tasks
general_tips: Harness engineering makes the same model far more useful by improving its environment, not just its inputs
Production AI agents need explicit recovery paths and feedback loops to avoid silent errors
skills.relevance: As prompt engineering matures, harness engineering is becoming the key competitive differentiator for building reliable production AI agents.

skills.description: A foundational agent design pattern that combines ReAct (Reasoning + Acting — alternating between thought steps and tool actions) with RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation — retrieving relevant context before generating). Together they enable AI agents to reason step-by-step, retrieve external knowledge, and act on real data.
skills.use_case: Building AI agents that need to reason through multi-step problems while accessing external knowledge sources
skills.output: AI agent that can reason, retrieve relevant documents/data, and act on real tools — not just generate text
tips: ReAct = alternate Thought steps (reasoning) with Action steps (tool calls) in a loop
RAG = retrieve relevant context from a knowledge base before generating the response
The progression is: basic LLM → LLM + Workflow (scripted) → true AI Agent (dynamic reasoning)
general_tips: AI agents differ from workflows because they decide which tools to call dynamically, not follow a fixed script
skills.relevance: ReAct and RAG are the two most fundamental techniques for building AI agents that go beyond simple chat to real knowledge retrieval and autonomous action.
